comment: Reviewed accepted code clones for the duplication gate (G17). A genuinely-irreducible repetition goes here as {"fingerprint": "<12-hex from the gate output>", "reason": "..."}. Keyed by content fingerprint, so an accepted clone stays accepted after it moves lines. Write-guard-protected and listed in check-gate-integrity's ESCAPE_LISTS: widening it must be COMMITTED, so it appears in the PR diff under CODEOWNERS. The seeded entries below are the web/native design-system mirror — the ONE deliberate dual implementation in the scaffold. Everything else must be extracted, not exempted.

allow.reason: design-system/EmptyState.tsx vs design-system-native/EmptyState.tsx — the deliberate web/native mirror. The two design systems share a variant CONTRACT (identical variant and option names, so a feature can move a screen between surfaces) but cannot share an implementation: web is Tailwind v4, mobile is Tailwind v3 via NativeWind 4, and the two majors do not share a class vocabulary. See the header of design-system-native/src/variants.ts for the full rationale.

design-system/Field.tsx vs design-system-native/Field.tsx — the same web/native mirror. React Native has no cascade and no pseudo-classes, so the web's `focus-visible:` / `placeholder:` / `disabled:` variants have no native equivalent; the native side expresses them as props and conditional classes.

design-system/Input.tsx vs design-system-native/Input.tsx (first region) — the same web/native mirror. The box models differ: RN flex defaults to column and has no `inline-flex`, so layout intent that the web inherits must be stated explicitly on the native side.
design-system/Input.tsx vs design-system-native/Input.tsx (second region) — same mirror, same reason as 4bdbc117162b.

design-system/index.ts vs design-system-native/index.ts — the two public barrels. They export the SAME names by design; that symmetry is the parity contract, and collapsing the barrels would put DOM components on the mobile import graph, which the boundary rules forbid.

design-system/variants.ts vs design-system-native/variants.ts (the cva card/input region) — the mirror's core. design-system-native/src/variants.ts documents in-source why this is deliberately NOT an import of the web file: differing Tailwind majors, no RN cascade or pseudo-classes, and differing box models. The variant names are the contract; the class strings cannot be shared.

apps/mobile/src/i18n/catalog.ts vs apps/web/lib/i18n/catalog.ts — the PluralMessage/Message declaration, which both seams need and neither can import. The clone is the TYPE PREAMBLE, not the copy: the tokenizer normalizes string literals, so the entries themselves fall below the threshold and only the eight-line CLDR-category interface matches (verified by collapsing it to one line — the gate goes clean). It is load-bearing on both surfaces: each `resolve()` selects a branch via Intl.PluralRules and needs the shape, so deleting it from either side removes plural support rather than duplication. WHY IT CANNOT BE EXTRACTED, and this is a property of the harness rather than of this file: every shared package source root — packages/contracts, packages/platform/*, packages/api, packages/design-tokens — is SEEDED, so `update` can never deliver a new export into an existing install. Extracting the type would compile on a fresh scaffold and break `types` on every consumer who adopted the web i18n seam, and the only remedy would be asking them to re-adopt packages/contracts/src/index.ts — the file most likely to carry their own domain schemas. Eight lines of pure type in two places is the smaller cost. The variant names are the contract, exactly as with the design-system mirror above; here the CLDR categories are.
